settings.label: Theme
settings.desc: Pick a look; each one has a dark and a light version.

settings.label: Light or dark
settings.desc: Switches the chosen theme between its light and dark versions.

settings.label: Wallpaper
settings.desc: Shows behind the panels in every look. Its light or dark print follows the look. Look's own keeps each look's own background: Ribbons in Glass and the chosen scene in NieR Mode. Choosing a NieR background later sets this back to Look's own.

settings.label: Accent color
settings.desc: The color of selections, focus outlines and progress; the first keeps the theme's own.

settings.label: Light Or Dark (Basic Theme)
settings.desc: Picks light, dark, or follow-your-computer coloring when the Basic Modern theme is active. Switches live, no restart. (Superseded by general.visual.theme-mode)

settings.label: Preview Themes Before Applying
settings.desc: Retired by Jared on 2026-10-13: no visible timed or hover-applied app-theme preview remains, and stored values are ignored. The internal Settings transaction preview/apply still validates and commits an activated theme choice. (Superseded by SSYS-010 and F3-084, DL-200)

settings.label: NieR Mode
settings.desc: Paints the whole app in NieR: Automata's ink and parchment, in light or dark. Your theme comes back when you turn it off.

settings.label: Customize NieR Mode
settings.desc: Choose which pieces of the look, motion, sound and world are installed.

settings.label: NieR background
settings.desc: A faint ink scene behind the app, or plain parchment.

settings.label: Customize Pip
settings.desc: Choose Pip’s optional chat and setup appearances, faces, motion, look and sound. Presets Full, Quiet, Still and Plain edit the same list; brand and loaders stay available. Labels and presets: Plans/pip_parts.json (S1–S9).

settings.label: Glass Background
settings.desc: Compatibility lineage only; never rendered or written. Wallpaper replaces Mesh/Depth/Minimal; SP-333 owns migration. (Superseded by SSYS-054 at the 2026-10-15 Liquid Glass/wallpaper publication.)

settings.label: How see-through panels are
settings.desc: Text always stays readable, whatever you choose.

settings.label: Retro textures
settings.desc: Pixel grid, paper and scanline overlays on Retro themes.

settings.label: Size of everything
settings.desc: Makes the whole app bigger or smaller.

settings.label: Text size
settings.desc: Base size of text in the app; code has its own size.

settings.label: Spacing
settings.desc: Automatic adapts to the size of your window.

settings.label: Reduce motion
settings.desc: Stops decorative movement; everything still works the same.

settings.label: Animation speed
settings.desc: How quickly panels and pages move.

settings.label: Chat Layout
settings.desc: Where the assistant chat lived: Docked to the right edge of the window, Overlay sliding above your work, or Detached as its own floating window. Retired with no options: a stored Overlay or Detached value is ignored and cleared on first read, with no pop-out and no notice, and the chat always starts in its column. (Superseded by the chat's fixed column and its Pop out, cmd.panel.undock, which lasts only while the app runs, DL-180, DL-187)

settings.label: High contrast
settings.desc: Stronger colors and edges, for the Basic theme.

settings.label: App font
settings.desc: Retro themes use display fonts; pick your computer's to use its everyday fonts.

settings.label: Your own themes
settings.desc: Create, import or export your own theme files.

settings.label: Start custom themes from
settings.desc: Colors you leave out come from this theme.

settings.label: Retro pixel grid strength
settings.desc: Zero hides the grid.

settings.label: Retro scanline strength
settings.desc: Zero hides the scanlines.

settings.label: Border width
settings.desc: Thickness of panel and control borders.

settings.label: Corner roundness
settings.desc: How rounded corners are.

settings.label: Line spacing
settings.desc: Space between lines of text.

settings.label: Scrollbar width
settings.desc: How wide scrollbars are.

settings.label: Extra padding
settings.desc: Fine-tunes space inside panels, on top of Spacing.

settings.label: Keyboard focus outline
settings.desc: How the outline around the focused control looks.

settings.label: How the app talks to me
settings.desc: Plain English hides jargon and rarely used controls.

settings.label: Explain terms in the chat I have open
settings.desc: Only that chat; change it in the chat's Explain simply sheet. The inventory keeps the run-scoped override identity, but Settings draws no current-chat control (SSYS-042, SSYS-055).

settings.label: Show hints when I hover
settings.desc: Shows hover hints on buttons and controls so you can learn what things do without clicking them.

settings.label: Keep running when I close the window
settings.desc: It hides in the system tray so work keeps going.

settings.label: Notifications
settings.desc: Off means nothing alerts you. You check the app yourself.

settings.label: Pop-up style
settings.desc: How alerts appear inside this app.

settings.label: Only important events
settings.desc: Approvals, finished runs, failures and rate limits.

settings.label: Play sounds
settings.desc: Short, quiet sounds when you send, when the answer arrives, and for approvals, completions and errors. The sounds of setup, the Guided Tour and NieR Mode follow it too. The speaker button in the chat header turns them off in one click.

settings.label: Sound library
settings.desc: Listen to the built-in sounds and your own.

settings.label: Key that sends a message
settings.desc: Ctrl+Enter avoids sending a half-typed message.

settings.label: New chats start in
settings.desc: Ask only answers, Agent makes changes, Plan thinks first. What Agent may do is set in Permissions.

settings.label: Scroll with new messages
settings.desc: Keeps chat scrolled to the newest message. If you scroll up to read, a jump-to-latest badge appears instead.

settings.label: Mark where I stopped reading
settings.desc: Shows a sticky marker at the last message you read when you've scrolled away, so you never lose your place.

settings.label: Copy button on code
settings.desc: Puts an always-visible copy button on every code block in chat, so grabbing code takes one click.

settings.label: Edit and resend my last message
settings.desc: Lets you fix and resend your most recent chat message instead of retyping it.

settings.label: Ask me questions as cards
settings.desc: Choices and a text box instead of a wall of text.

settings.label: Keep half-written answers
settings.desc: Closing a question card never loses what you typed.

settings.label: Show a space meter in each chat
settings.desc: A small meter in each chat shows how full its working space is.

settings.label: Show what the assistant does
settings.desc: Cards for commands, web searches and file edits.

settings.label: Show when it reads files
settings.desc: Safety and approval messages always show.

settings.label: Draw diagrams
settings.desc: Diagram code in chat shows as a picture.

settings.label: Interactive charts and previews
settings.desc: Small sandboxed widgets that can't touch your files.

settings.label: Change modes by asking
settings.desc: Say "use plan mode" to switch in the middle of a chat.

settings.label: Show what helpers are doing
settings.desc: A line in chat for each helper at work.

settings.label: Say when a different model answered
settings.desc: Nothing swaps without you seeing it.

settings.label: Picture buttons in the message box
settings.desc: Shown when the current model can use them.

settings.label: Let me point at things to share with chat
settings.desc: Nothing is sent until you confirm.

settings.label: Find this project's languages automatically
settings.desc: Shows which languages the project uses and suggests the tools that fit.

settings.label: Hide ignored files
settings.desc: Hides build output and other ignored files; off dims them.

settings.label: Show the open file in the file tree
settings.desc: Automatically scrolls and expands the file tree to show whichever file you're editing.

settings.label: Search all settings
settings.desc: Takes you to the search box at the top of Settings.

settings.label: Show where each setting comes from
settings.desc: Labels each setting with its scope (Global, Project, Persona…) and which layer won, so overrides aren't a mystery.

settings.label: Dashboard widgets
settings.desc: Opens the dashboard's widget picker on Home.

settings.label: Order of the icons on the left
settings.desc: Drag to reorder the icons in the left activity bar per project, so your most-used panels sit on top.

settings.label: Show names next to those icons
settings.desc: Shows each destination's name beside its icon in the activity bar. It mirrors the bar's own expand and collapse control in both directions.
search: Show Names Next to the Icons on the Left

settings.label: Show words in the status bar’s agent and process counts
settings.desc: Numbers shows glyph and number pairs with full words on hover. Turn this on for words beside the counts. Questions and process input stay separate (D5).

settings.label: Check spelling
settings.desc: In chat and notes; code is never marked.

settings.label: Languages to check
settings.desc: Every language you write in; words valid in any of them are accepted.

settings.label: Words to always accept
settings.desc: Names and terms the spell checker should not flag.

settings.label: Panel Position
settings.desc: Whether side panels like Chat and File Manager sit docked to an edge or float as separate windows, per project. (Superseded by the chat's Pop out, cmd.panel.undock, and the left rail's side panels, DL-180)

settings.label: Keep hidden features findable
settings.desc: Hidden features still appear in search and commands.

settings.label: Show
settings.desc: Whether the History view lists only the current project's runs or everything across all projects.

settings.label: Approved only
settings.desc: Shows only approved work in History by default; 'All history' expands to drafts and rejected items too.

settings.label: Include archived
settings.desc: Also lists archived runs and plans in History, which can make long lists noisier.

settings.label: Compare two versions
settings.desc: Opens from an item in the timeline.

settings.label: If I send while it is busy
settings.desc: Wait holds your message until the current step is done; Steer sends it into the running reply at once.

settings.label: Messages that can wait
settings.desc: When the line is full, new messages must wait.

settings.label: Alert me about
settings.desc: Fewer levels means fewer interruptions.

settings.label: Destinations
settings.desc: Kept in step with the Destinations list.

settings.label: Where each event goes
settings.desc: Kept in step with each event's destinations.

settings.label: Add a sound
settings.desc: Upload a file or import a pack.

settings.label: Sound for each event
settings.desc: Kept in step with the Event sounds list.

settings.label: Stop repeating a warning after
settings.desc: Minutes of calm. Urgent and blocked alerts always repeat.

settings.label: Ask for a reason when I dismiss an alert
settings.desc: Leaves a note you can look back on.

settings.label: Explain grayed-out controls right away
settings.desc: Automatically pops up an explanation when you hit a disabled control. The manual 'Explain this' option always exists.

settings.label: Most editor tabs open at once
settings.desc: Past it, the editor tab you used least recently closes. Pinned tabs and tabs with unsaved changes stay, and other kinds of tab don't count.

settings.label: Preview Tabs
settings.desc: A single click on a file opens it in the panel's one preview tab, shown in italics, which your next single click replaces; a double click, an edit or dragging the tab keeps it. Off: every file you open gets a tab of its own.

settings.label: Tab Sizing
settings.desc: Shrink to fit: tabs are 96 to 200 px wide and, when they no longer fit, shrink to 72 px and then to icons before the rest move to the +N list. Fixed width: tabs keep their width and the ones that do not fit move to the +N list at once. The tab you are in always stays visible and at least 120 px wide.

settings.label: Keep the Chat Open in Narrow Windows
settings.desc: When the room left for your panels drops below 480 px, the chat folds to a thin strip at the edge so the panels stay usable. On keeps the chat open instead. Retired before it shipped: the switch is the chat's own, in its header menu and the title bar's Home menu, not a Settings row. (Superseded by Keep the chat open in narrow windows in the chat's header menu, ui.chat_column.keep_open, DL-187)

settings.label: History in new workspaces
settings.desc: Start History as a flyout or pinned beside the messages in a workspace with no saved choice. Changing this never changes History in a workspace already open; its pin stays with its layout.

settings.label: Most files listed per folder
settings.desc: Stops giant folders from freezing the app.

settings.label: If a dropped file has the same name
settings.desc: What happens when a drag-and-drop hits an existing filename: ask you, overwrite, or keep both with a rename.

settings.label: Dragging files
settings.desc: Hold Shift while dragging to do the other.

settings.label: Remember open folders
settings.desc: Remembers which folders you had open in the file tree for each project between sessions.

settings.label: Archive chats untouched for
settings.desc: In days. 0 never archives.

settings.label: Deleted chats can be restored for
settings.desc: In days.

settings.label: Show technical details in chats
settings.desc: Session ids and branch history; for troubleshooting.

settings.label: Progress graph opens on
settings.desc: What the graph of a Goal shows when you open it in the assistant chat.

settings.label: Graph detail
settings.desc: How much of a Goal's steps the graph draws.

settings.label: Progress view layout
settings.desc: Which panels a Goal's progress view shows, and where.

settings.label: Export history
settings.desc: A file of sessions and events; secrets left out.

settings.label: Rebuild history search
settings.desc: When results look wrong or incomplete.

settings.label: Reset the layout
settings.desc: Puts panels back; open files, terminals and chats stay.

settings.label: Show first-run tips
settings.desc: Short tips the first time you use each part of the app.

settings.label: First screen when Puppet Master opens
settings.desc: The page you land on; the side panel is chosen below.

settings.label: Side panel when a project opens
settings.desc: Which side panel greets you when a project opens — your last-used one, or always the same panel.

settings.label: Remember window size and layout
settings.desc: Size, position, panel widths and splits come back as you left them.

settings.label: Bring my work back after a crash
settings.desc: Brings back your terminals, editors, and chats automatically if the app crashes, so you pick up where you left off.

settings.label: Protect unsaved changes
settings.desc: Keeps copies of unsaved edits so a crash can't lose them.

settings.label: Tabs reopened next time
settings.desc: Tabs of every kind. The ones you used least recently are left out first, and each panel's open tab and pinned tabs always come back.

settings.label: Starting Layout
settings.desc: The layout a workspace opens in when it has no saved layout of its own: Home (a dashboard and your files over a row for terminals and tools), Build, Terminals 2x2 (four terminals) or Focus (one panel). Changing it never rearranges panels that are already open; Restore Home Layout still returns to Home.

settings.label: Re-check the debug setup when a debugging chat resumes
settings.desc: Catches a changed program or debugger before it runs again.

settings.label: Your AI services
settings.desc: Connect, re-check, or disconnect your AI accounts. Everything else needs at least one working connection here.

settings.label: GitHub account
settings.desc: Sign in to GitHub so Puppet Master can create branches and pull requests for you. Disconnect removes the saved token.

settings.label: Which account goes first
settings.desc: Each service's account list is in its page under Services.

option_labels.Pick per provider: The one I pick for each service

settings.label: Use this account
settings.desc: Turn an account off to keep it saved but skip it when choosing who runs your work. Nothing is deleted.

settings.label: Account nickname
settings.desc: A friendly name so you can tell accounts apart, like 'Work Claude' or 'Personal'.

settings.label: Use an account for the next run
settings.desc: Force a specific account for the current or next run — handy when testing or when one account is running low.

settings.label: How a Claude account signs in
settings.desc: How your Claude account signs in. Subscription and console logins have different limits and billing.

settings.label: ChatGPT plan or OpenAI API key
settings.desc: ChatGPT plan and API key are separate quota pools with separate bills — set up each one you use.

settings.label: Preferred way to sign in
settings.desc: Whether a provider uses an API key, browser login, or its own default. Only methods the provider supports are offered.

settings.label: Switch accounts by themselves
settings.desc: The shared setting: when one account hits its limit, the next one carries on. A service with its own choice uses that instead.

settings.label: Use OpenCode
settings.desc: Turn on the OpenCode engine as an extra way to run AI work. Off means its servers and models stay hidden.

settings.label: Add an OpenCode server
settings.desc: Let Puppet Master start and manage a server for you, or attach to one you already run yourself.

settings.label: Server address
settings.desc: Where the OpenCode server lives, like http://127.0.0.1:4096. Wrong address means models never appear.

settings.label: Anthropic API key
settings.desc: Added and replaced in Anthropic API, under Providers & Accounts.

settings.label: OpenAI API key
settings.desc: Added and replaced in ChatGPT / Codex, under Providers & Accounts.

settings.label: Gemini API key
settings.desc: Added and replaced in Gemini API, under Providers & Accounts.

settings.label: Cursor API key
settings.desc: Added and replaced in Cursor, under Providers & Accounts.

settings.label: MiniMax API key
settings.desc: Added and replaced in MiniMax Coding Plan, under Providers & Accounts.

settings.label: Access token
settings.desc: Kept in the system keychain; used for extra GitHub features.

settings.label: GitHub servers allowed
settings.desc: Whether company-hosted GitHub Enterprise servers may be used, or only github.com. Enterprise repos show as disabled otherwise.

settings.label: Sign-in return address
settings.desc: Must be this computer, such as 127.0.0.1.

settings.label: Where an account's key is kept
settings.desc: Where each account's secret lives — your system keychain (safest), an environment variable, a file, or the provider's CLI.

settings.label: How an account's key is sent
settings.desc: The technical way a credential is attached to requests. Only change if a provider's docs tell you to.

settings.label: Account type
settings.desc: Whether an account is a subscription, API key, browser login, or CLI-managed. Affects how limits and resets are counted.

settings.label: Stick to a chosen account
settings.desc: Whether work may use a different account than the one you chose.

settings.label: Account for one run
settings.desc: Explicitly name the account a run should use, separate from the general binding policy.

settings.label: Account order
settings.desc: Lower numbers get picked first. Ties go to the account already doing the work, so runs stay stable.

settings.label: Switch at a natural break
settings.desc: Moves between tasks when quota runs low, not in the middle of one.

settings.label: Warn when this much is left
settings.desc: The shared heads-up before an account runs low. A service can have its own.

settings.label: Switch when this much is left
settings.desc: The shared level: below this, work moves to the next account. A service, or one account, can have its own.

settings.label: Per-Account Switch Override
settings.desc: Give one account its own switch trigger, different from the global level — useful for small trial accounts. (Superseded by ai.accounts.hard-switch-level at scope account)

settings.label: How an account shares work
settings.desc: Sticky stays on one account, fallback only moves when forced, round-robin spreads work evenly.

settings.label: Rest after a rate limit
settings.desc: How long an account rests after hitting a rate limit before it's tried again: the provider's own default, or 5, 15, 30 or 60 minutes. Provider defaults are usually right.

settings.label: Retries before an account rests
settings.desc: How many times a struggling account is retried before it's benched, so one flaky account can't stall everything.

settings.label: Quota profile
settings.desc: Which provider quota plan an account follows — sets how usage and reset windows are tracked for it.

settings.label: Jobs an account may do
settings.desc: Limit an account to certain kinds of work, or block it from some — e.g. keep an expensive account off routine tasks.

settings.label: Google Cloud project
settings.desc: For Gemini accounts: which Google Cloud project gets billed and whose quota applies.

settings.label: Who is billed for an account
settings.desc: Pick the org, team, or personal context charged for this account. Costs are tracked per billing entity.

settings.label: Switch history
settings.desc: Read-only log of every automatic account switch and why it happened — good for 'why did my bill change?' questions.

settings.label: Server password
settings.desc: Only if the server asks for one. Separate from any model keys inside OpenCode.

settings.label: Server controls
settings.desc: Reconnect, restart (managed only), refresh the model list, or detach a server from Puppet Master's control.

settings.label: Trust the model list for
settings.desc: How long the discovered model list is trusted before re-asking the server. Lower means fresher but chattier.

settings.label: OpenCode program location
settings.desc: Only used when the server cannot be reached directly.

settings.label: Skip Claude Code skills in OpenCode
settings.desc: Stops OpenCode loading Claude Code skills on its own. Puppet Master still routes its canonical skills either way.

settings.label: Everyday model
settings.desc: For chat, planning and research when nothing more specific is chosen.

settings.label: Service tried first
settings.desc: Used first when more than one service could do a job.

settings.label: Planning and supervising
settings.desc: Turns plans into work and supervises runs.

settings.label: Everyday building
settings.desc: The day-to-day building. A mid-range model keeps costs down.

settings.label: Design and layout
settings.desc: Screens, layout and look. Pick one with good taste.

settings.label: The hardest jobs
settings.desc: Big changes across the project and risky reasoning.

settings.label: Checking finished work
settings.desc: Checks finished work until it passes or is truly stuck.

settings.label: Speed or power
settings.desc: Faster and cheaper, or slower and smarter, without changing the model.

settings.label: Thinking depth
settings.desc: Deeper is smarter but slower and costs more.

settings.label: Explaining things to you
settings.desc: Answers "explain this to me". A cheaper model is fine.

settings.label: Use a service
settings.desc: Switch a whole provider off for future runs. Its accounts stay saved and can be switched back on anytime.

settings.label: Goals: doing the work
settings.desc: Runs autonomous Goals.

settings.label: Goals: checking the work
settings.desc: Checks Goal results. Kept apart from the worker.

settings.label: Work lanes
settings.desc: Pin each work lane (cheap executor, reviewer, orchestrator, verifier, adjudicator, certifier) to a provider, account, and model.

settings.label: Role rules
settings.desc: Advanced mapping of roles (worker default, planner, evaluator) and provider capability-level defaults, stored apart from the pickers above.

settings.label: Helper agents
settings.desc: Never bigger than the agent that started it.

settings.label: Helper agents' thinking depth
settings.desc: How hard each helper thinks.

settings.label: Service for each lane
settings.desc: Choose a different AI platform for each work lane — seams, packages, lanes, and nodes can each run somewhere else.

settings.label: Model for each lane
settings.desc: An exact model name for one kind of work, written the way its service writes it. Blank uses the lane's service default.

settings.label: Role for one run

settings.label: Original project
settings.desc: Address or owner/name of the project you contribute to.

settings.label: Make my own copy (fork)
settings.desc: Makes your own copy of the upstream repo automatically via GitHub so you can propose changes without write access.

settings.label: My copy
settings.desc: Filled in once the copy exists.

settings.label: Branch for my changes
settings.desc: The branch your pull-request work goes on when contributing to another project, e.g. feature/add-x.

settings.label: How finished work is merged
settings.desc: Auto follows your project's convention; merge keeps history, squash makes one tidy commit, rebase replays commits. Merge is safest.

settings.label: Send commits online
settings.desc: Manual means you push when ready; auto pushes after each successful merge; never keeps everything local until you say so.

settings.label: Overwrite history online (force push)
settings.desc: Force pushes can overwrite others' work. Never is safest; with-lease refuses if someone else pushed first; always is risky.

settings.label: Safety level
settings.desc: One dial for how carefully branches and recovery are handled.

settings.label: Branch naming style
settings.desc: The workflow convention used when naming new branches — feature branches, hotfixes, releases, trunk-based, or your own scheme.

option_labels.Feature: One branch per piece of work

settings.label: Custom branch pattern
settings.desc: Use {node} and {id}, e.g. work/{node}-{id}.

settings.label: Name on your changes
settings.desc: Recorded on every change saved to history; anyone who can see the history sees it.

settings.label: Email on your changes
settings.desc: Code services use it to link changes to your account. Their private no-reply address keeps yours out of public history.

settings.label: How Git signs in
settings.desc: For each code service: a token from signing in, or one of your SSH keys. Separate from the website sign-in.

settings.label: SSH key Git uses
settings.desc: For each code service that signs in with an SSH key: which key from your SSH key list.

settings.label: Sign your changes
settings.desc: Some projects only accept signed changes.

settings.label: Signing key
settings.desc: The key that signs your changes while signing is on.

settings.label: Store big files separately
settings.desc: Keeps big files out of the normal history with Git LFS, so the project stays small and fast.

settings.label: Big file size
settings.desc: Files larger than this are stored separately.

settings.label: Always store these separately
settings.desc: File patterns such as *.psd or *.mp4, whatever their size.

settings.label: Never saved in history
settings.desc: Written to the ignore list of every new repository: secrets, dependencies and build output.

settings.label: Protected branches
settings.desc: Never overwritten; changes go through a review. * matches anything, so release/* covers every release branch.

settings.label: Workspace folder
settings.desc: The folder on disk where private AI workspaces are created. Move it if your default drive is short on space.

settings.label: Give each new chat its own workspace
settings.desc: Gives each new chat its own branch and workspace on the first message, so experiments never touch your main files until merged.

settings.label: Chat workspaces start from
settings.desc: The branch new chat workspaces are created from. Normally inherits your main branch — override for long-lived feature work.

settings.label: This chat's workspace
settings.desc: Opens from a chat.

settings.label: File browser follows the open chat
settings.desc: The file browser shows the files of whichever chat workspace you're in, so you always look at the version being edited.

settings.label: Test command
settings.desc: Leave empty to find it automatically.

settings.label: Time limit
settings.desc: 30 to 1800 seconds.

settings.label: What gets tested
settings.desc: Merged result tests your branch combined with the latest main — catches clashes early. Branch only is faster but can miss them.

settings.label: Warn me at this many workspaces
settings.desc: 0 turns the warning off.

settings.label: Give up creating a workspace after
settings.desc: In seconds, 5 to 300.

settings.label: Fix a stuck branch or workspace
settings.desc: Guided recovery for tangled merges, orphaned workspaces, and other git trouble — undo safely instead of typing git commands.

settings.label: Keep check results up to date
settings.desc: Keeps pinned workflow statuses current using event updates plus an occasional poll, so you don't have to hit refresh.

settings.label: Also remove ignored files when cleaning
settings.desc: Extends cleanup to gitignored files like caches and local configs. Off by default because those files can be hard to recreate.
search: Also Delete Ignored Files on Cleanup

settings.label: Delete build output after runs
settings.desc: Removes known build folders (like target/) when a run ends to reclaim disk space, at the cost of slower rebuilds next time.

settings.label: Remove every workspace
settings.desc: Unmerged work in them is lost.

settings.label: Keep test run logs for
settings.desc: Blank keeps them until you delete them.

settings.label: Keep only the last runs' logs
settings.desc: Blank means no limit.
search: Or Keep Only the Last N Runs

settings.label: Use crews
settings.desc: Several personas on one Goal. Uses noticeably more credits.

settings.label: Default lineup
settings.desc: Personas in a new crew, in order.

settings.label: Crews running at once, at most
settings.desc: The server may allow fewer.

settings.label: Agents in one crew, at most
settings.desc: The server may allow fewer.

settings.label: Use helper agents
settings.desc: Off means one agent does everything.

settings.label: Let helpers work side by side
settings.desc: Lets helpers work side by side in separate workspaces instead of taking turns. Faster, but heavier on your machine and budget.

settings.label: Helpers at once, at most
settings.desc: The server may allow fewer.

settings.label: Split work only when it's this big
settings.desc: Work with fewer parts than this stays with one agent.
search: Split Work Only When Big Enough

settings.label: Reading per helper, at most
settings.desc: In tokens; keeps costs predictable.

settings.label: If a helper fails
settings.desc: Whether failed helpers get another try. Bounded retries gives a couple of attempts; backoff waits longer between tries.

settings.label: Always use helpers
settings.desc: Usually best left off.

settings.label: One Writer at a Time
settings.desc: Only one agent may change files at any moment, preventing two helpers from overwriting each other's edits.

settings.label: Extra write protection
settings.desc: Optionally restrict helpers further: only the lead writes, helpers propose patches, or each helper gets its own isolated workspace.

option_labels.isolated worktree per subagent: Each helper gets its own copy

settings.label: Helpers for each kind of step
settings.desc: Choose exactly which helpers run at each step type (seam, package, lane, iteration). Empty lists let the app choose automatically.

settings.label: Always include
settings.desc: Helpers that join every run no matter what. This list wins even over the excluded list below.

settings.label: Never use
settings.desc: Helpers excluded from automatic selection — useful when one keeps getting picked but never helps your project.

settings.label: Requests to one AI service at once
settings.desc: The server may allow fewer.

settings.label: Agents active at once, at most
settings.desc: The server may allow fewer.

settings.label: Delegation levels, hard stop
settings.desc: No helper goes deeper than this, whatever else says.

settings.label: Agents per run, at most
settings.desc: The emergency brake on runaway helpers.

settings.label: Helpers may hire their own helpers
settings.desc: 0 = no; each level adds cost.

settings.label: View Agent Permissions Snapshot
settings.desc: Shows the frozen rulebook each agent gets before its first call: autonomy, what it may write, model policy, tool limits, budgets.

settings.label: View Helper Work Contract
settings.desc: Opens from a running Goal.

settings.label: Keep Helper Memory Separate
settings.desc: Each helper keeps its own context and cache, and its errors surface as clean failures instead of corrupting the main run.

settings.label: Track Imported Agents' Origins
settings.desc: Records where outside agents came from, what they were allowed to do, and their transcripts — an audit trail for borrowed help.

settings.label: Service that makes pictures
settings.desc: Only services you are signed in to can be chosen.

option_labels.OpenAI gpt-image-2: GPT Image 2 with an OpenAI API key

settings.label: Model for each ability
settings.desc: Each ability's Uses row picks it. The service's default model is the usual choice.

option_labels.Per-task override: A model I choose per ability

settings.label: Model nicknames
settings.desc: Short names you can type instead of a full model name.

settings.label: Accept pictures and files
settings.desc: Off keeps every conversation text only.

settings.label: Hand back files and media
settings.desc: Off means answers come back as text only.

settings.label: Voice typing
settings.desc: What you say becomes a draft you check before sending.

settings.label: Understand pictures and screenshots
settings.desc: Works even when your main model cannot see pictures.

settings.label: Where to look for 'my screenshot'
settings.desc: Used when you mention a screenshot without attaching it.

settings.label: Which picture wins
settings.desc: Used when more than one picture could match a request.

settings.label: Backup for looking at pictures
settings.desc: Which model steps in when your usual vision model is down or unavailable. 'Auto' picks the best available one for you.

settings.label: If private details can't be blurred
settings.desc: Blocking the picture is safest.

settings.label: Keep results for
settings.desc: After that, results are cleaned up.

settings.label: Results folder
settings.desc: Inside your project. Each ability saves to a folder here.

settings.label: Let the assistant make media
settings.desc: Pictures, video, speech and music. Off by default.

settings.label: Kinds of media it may make
settings.desc: Choose which media kinds are allowed: images, screenshots, diagrams, recordings, video. Anything off reports 'disabled by admin' to tools.

settings.label: Make videos
settings.desc: Not every service can. One that cannot says so.

settings.label: Read text aloud
settings.desc: Your workspace may lock this off on some plans.

settings.label: Make music and sounds
settings.desc: Songs, instrumentals, beats and sound effects. Off by default.

settings.label: Picture shape
settings.desc: You can still ask for another shape in a request.

settings.label: Picture size
settings.desc: Bigger looks sharper but costs more and takes longer.

settings.label: Picture quality
settings.desc: Draft is fast and cheap. High takes longer and costs more.

settings.label: Pictures per request
settings.desc: 1 to 8. Each extra picture costs credits.

settings.label: Video length
settings.desc: 0.5 to 60 seconds. Longer takes longer and costs more.

settings.label: Video sharpness
settings.desc: Sharpness of generated video. This wins over any pixel-size hint when both are given.

settings.label: Voice
settings.desc: Which voice reads generated speech aloud. Pick one that suits your project's tone.

settings.label: Picture file type
settings.desc: PNG keeps every detail. JPG and WebP make smaller files.

settings.label: How pictures come back
settings.desc: Get images back as a link or as embedded data. Heads-up: MiniMax links expire after 24 hours, so download what you want to keep.

settings.label: Same picture every time
settings.desc: Set a number to repeat a result. Blank gives a new one.

settings.label: Let MiniMax improve my prompt
settings.desc: Off keeps your exact words.

settings.label: Music tempo
settings.desc: Beats per minute, 60 to 200. 120 suits most styles.

settings.label: Extra options for the service
settings.desc: Leave empty unless a guide tells you what to add.

settings.label: Search the web
settings.desc: Off stops every web search, in chat and in /web.
search: Let the AI Search the Web

settings.label: Order services are tried
settings.desc: Used when an ability has no order of its own.

settings.label: Service status
settings.desc: Connected, needs a key, or failed recently. Read only.

settings.label: Show error details
settings.desc: Adds each service's last failure message to the list.

settings.label: DuckDuckGo (free backup)
settings.desc: Basic, free search used when other services can't answer.

settings.label: Firecrawl
settings.desc: Reads difficult sites. Needs a key or your own server.

settings.label: Firecrawl key
settings.desc: From firecrawl.dev. Kept in your server's keychain.

settings.label: Firecrawl address
settings.desc: Use your own Firecrawl server instead of the cloud one.

settings.label: Exa
settings.desc: Strong at search and deep research. Needs a key.

settings.label: Tavily
settings.desc: Searches, reads and extracts pages. Needs a key.

settings.label: How deeply Tavily reads
settings.desc: Deeper reading costs more per page.

settings.label: Brave Search
settings.desc: An independent search index. Needs a key.

settings.label: Jina Reader
settings.desc: Reads pages other services can't. Needs a key.

settings.label: Your AI model's own web search
settings.desc: Uses your model account, no extra key. Tried last.

settings.label: Which service does each job
settings.desc: The first choice and the backups for each ability.

settings.label: Service keys
settings.desc: Add, replace or remove a web service's key.

settings.label: How PDFs are read
settings.desc: Scanned PDFs need the slower reader.

settings.label: Results per search
settings.desc: More results give broader answers but cost more.

settings.label: Most websites per research task
settings.desc: Caps how many different sites a research task pulls from, keeping deep-dives fast and affordable.

settings.label: Pages read before asking you
settings.desc: Research asks before opening more than this.

settings.label: Most pages per crawl
settings.desc: Caps pages fetched when crawling a whole site. The app's cap (25) deliberately overrides Firecrawl's huge 10,000-page default.

settings.label: How many links deep a crawl goes
settings.desc: How many clicks away from the starting page a crawl may wander. Deeper crawls find more but take much longer.

settings.label: Most pages in a site outline
settings.desc: Caps pages listed when mapping a site's structure (listing URLs without reading them).

settings.label: How many links deep an outline goes
settings.desc: How deep site mapping follows links when listing a site's pages.

settings.label: Time limit per page
settings.desc: Seconds to wait for one page before giving up.

settings.label: Ask before spending more than
settings.desc: In credits. Bigger web jobs wait for your OK.

settings.label: Never spend more than
settings.desc: In credits. Bigger jobs stop unless you approve that one.

settings.label: Let Firecrawl reuse its saved copies
settings.desc: Off keeps pages freshest.

settings.label: Space for saved web pages
settings.desc: The oldest pages are dropped when it's full.

settings.label: Keep search results for
settings.desc: After this they are fetched again.

settings.label: Keep pages for
settings.desc: How long saved page content stays fresh before being re-fetched.

settings.label: Keep crawls and outlines for
settings.desc: How long saved crawl and site-map results stay fresh. Longest lifetime, since site structure rarely changes.

settings.label: Get past site blocking
settings.desc: How aggressively Firecrawl dodges site blocking. Basic is cheapest; enhanced costs +4 credits per page. Cloud only.

settings.label: Browser profile
settings.desc: Protected sign-in windows never keep anything.

settings.label: Remember website logins
settings.desc: Keeps approved cookies for later runs.

settings.label: Let your own servers redirect
settings.desc: Where a self-hosted service may pass a request on to.

settings.label: Time limit for your own servers
settings.desc: Seconds before a slow self-hosted service is cut off.

settings.label: Proxy
settings.desc: Most people use this computer's settings.

settings.label: Proxy address (http)
settings.desc: Proxy for plain web traffic. Only used when Network Proxy is set to manual.

settings.label: Proxy address (https)
settings.desc: Proxy for secure web traffic. Only used when Network Proxy is set to manual.

settings.label: Sites that skip the proxy
settings.desc: Usually internal company addresses.

settings.label: Proxy sign-in
settings.desc: Only if your proxy asks for a name and password.

settings.label: Company certificate file
settings.desc: For networks that inspect secure traffic.

settings.label: Certificates for specific sites
settings.desc: Use a certificate only for the sites you list.

settings.label: Work offline
settings.desc: Blocks all internet use. Saved pages still work.

settings.label: Keep a search index of this project
settings.desc: Off stops indexing and clears what was built.

settings.label: How much to index
settings.desc: Deep finds more but uses more of your computer.

settings.label: Rebuild the index
settings.desc: Use it when search results look stale or wrong.

settings.label: Space used by the index
settings.desc: Shows how much space the index uses locally and (for remote projects) on the remote side, before you decide to clear it.

settings.label: Skip files larger than
settings.desc: Big files are left out of the index to keep it fast. Raise this only if you genuinely need to search huge files.

settings.label: Leave out of search
settings.desc: Folders and files to skip, on top of the built-in list.
search: Files to Leave Out of Search

settings.label: Follow linked folders
settings.desc: Linked folders must still be inside the project.

settings.label: Copy kept on this computer
settings.desc: Remote projects only: index a lighter copy locally first.

settings.label: Clear the index
settings.desc: Frees the space; search rebuilds it when needed.

settings.label: Default persona
settings.desc: Answers when you haven't picked one.

settings.label: Persona list
settings.desc: The list on the Personas tab is where personas are managed.

settings.label: Persona in one chat
settings.desc: Each chat shows who is answering in its persona chip; change it there for that chat only.

settings.label: Who picks the persona
settings.desc: Let the app choose the best character for each request, pick one yourself, or mix: auto-pick unless you override.

settings.label: Switch by asking
settings.desc: In any chat, say 'let the researcher handle this'.
search: Ask for a Persona in Plain Words

settings.label: Built-in personas
settings.desc: Nine locked personas that always work.

settings.label: Keep one persona for a whole chat
settings.desc: New chats stay with the persona they start with. A chat's own menu can change this for that chat.

settings.label: Hidden specialists
settings.desc: Bundled personas kept out of pickers.

settings.label: Save new personas for
settings.desc: Save new characters just for this project or for every project. Project-local personas override global ones with the same job.

settings.label: Name
settings.desc: Shown in pickers and in chat.

settings.label: What it is for
settings.desc: One line. It also helps automatic picking.

settings.label: Short id
settings.desc: Lowercase with dashes; used in files and automation.

settings.label: Tags
settings.desc: Help search and automatic picking find this persona.

settings.label: Other names it answers to
settings.desc: So 'ask the prof' reaches your teacher persona.

settings.label: Preferred model
settings.desc: The AI model this character uses when active. Leave empty to inherit whatever the project or app already picked.

settings.label: Answer style
settings.desc: The overall voice of this character: short and to the point, thorough, or somewhere in between.

settings.label: Chatter while working
settings.desc: Updates while it works; not the answer's length.

settings.label: Answer length
settings.desc: Fine-tunes Answer style.

settings.label: Answer format
settings.desc: Formatted text, data (JSON) or plain text.

settings.label: Starts by
settings.desc: How this character begins working: ask before acting, plan first, work normally, or run without pauses. Runs can still override it.

settings.label: Preferred AI service
settings.desc: Which AI service this character prefers, like Claude, Gemini Direct, or Antigravity CLI. Leave empty to inherit.

settings.label: Faster or smarter edition
settings.desc: Prefer the fast or the powerful edition of the chosen model family. Leave empty to inherit.

settings.label: Creativity
settings.desc: Higher is more inventive, less predictable.

settings.label: Word choice range
settings.desc: How far it looks past the likeliest words. Rarely needed; it stacks with Creativity.

settings.label: Thinking effort
settings.desc: How hard this character thinks before answering. More effort means smarter answers but slower and pricier runs.

settings.label: Spending cap
settings.desc: Over-budget models are skipped with a note. 0 = no cap.

settings.label: Reach for tools
settings.desc: How readily this persona uses tools.

settings.label: Tools it prefers
settings.desc: Tools this character reaches for first, like Site Reader for the web. Guidance only; permissions still apply.

settings.label: Tools it avoids
settings.desc: A nudge, not a ban. Use permissions to block a tool.

settings.label: Notes on using tools
settings.desc: When and how it should reach for its tools, in plain sentences.

settings.label: Instructions
settings.desc: The standing instructions it works from.

settings.label: Skills it carries
settings.desc: Skill packs loaded automatically whenever this character is active, so it always knows its specialty tricks.

settings.label: What it may do without asking
settings.desc: The named rule set deciding what this character may do without asking you first. Leave empty to inherit the project's rules.

settings.label: Plugins it ignores
settings.desc: Plugins this character ignores while working. They stay installed and keep running for everyone else.

settings.label: Mark settings a model can't follow
settings.desc: Marks each tuning control as fully, partly, or not supported by the current model, so you know which knobs actually work.

settings.label: See Which Settings Were Skipped
settings.desc: Opens a log of persona settings the model could not honor on recent runs, so surprises are never silent.

settings.label: Your Skills

settings.label: Skill on or off
settings.desc: Switch any single skill on or off without deleting it. Off skills stay installed but agents can't use them.

settings.label: Skills in chat
settings.desc: Type /skill in chat to browse and run skills, or just ask for one by name.

settings.label: Find new skills automatically
settings.desc: Looks in your project's and your profile's skill folders when Puppet Master starts.

settings.label: Rescan for Skills
settings.desc: Looks again in all skill folders right now — use after adding files by hand or pulling new project changes.

settings.label: Shown on each skill in the list
settings.desc: Whether it's ready, where it came from, and which personas use it.

settings.desc: Orders the skill list by name, where it came from, or its permission — remembered for the rest of this session.

settings.label: Search Skills
settings.desc: Type to narrow the skill list by name, description, source, readiness, or permission — handy once you have many installed.

settings.desc: Opens a read-only view of a skill's instructions so you can see exactly what it will do before letting it run.

settings.desc: Applies one permission to every skill matching a pattern (like doc-*) at once; shows how many will change before you confirm.

settings.desc: The assistant picks up a skill when it fits the job. Skills with a warning always wait for you.

settings.label: Turn new skills on right away
settings.desc: Off means a new skill arrives switched off until you've had a look at it.

settings.desc: Scans every skill for broken headers, name mismatches, or overlong descriptions and lists anything that needs fixing.

settings.label: Turn new plugins on right away
settings.desc: Off means a new plugin arrives switched off, so new code never runs before you've looked at it.

settings.label: Plugin packages

settings.label: When other apps have servers
settings.desc: Ask me first shows what was found before anything is added. Otherwise they're added switched off until you review them.

settings.label: Server Health & Logs
settings.desc: See when each server was last checked and its last error. Read-only — a quick way to tell why a tool stopped responding.

settings.label: Sign Out of a Server
settings.desc: Revokes a server's saved sign-in without deleting the server. Use this if credentials expire or you suspect a leak.

settings.label: How a server connects
settings.desc: The connection style for each server: a local program (stdio) or a web address (sse or http). Each server uses exactly one.

settings.label: How a program server starts
settings.desc: The command, arguments, folder, and environment used to start a local server. Wrong values here are the top cause of Install Failed.

settings.label: A web server's address
settings.desc: The web address for a remote server. Changing it wipes saved sign-ins for that server, so you will need to sign in again.

settings.label: Extra headers for a web server
settings.desc: Extra key-value headers sent to a remote server, usually an API key. Used by servers that skip the normal sign-in flow.

settings.label: Work out sign-in automatically
settings.desc: Turn off only for servers that use a plain key instead of signing in.

settings.label: Refresh a Server Sign-In
settings.desc: Forces a fresh sign-in token for a server right now. Handy when a server says Needs Auth but you already signed in.

settings.label: Where a server can be used
settings.desc: Whether a server is available everywhere, in one project, for one profile, or managed by another app (External). Each server has exactly one.

settings.label: Wait for a server this long
settings.desc: How long to wait for a server to start or answer before giving up.

settings.label: Describe tools only when they're used
settings.desc: Keeps each request small, so answers are faster and cheaper.
search: Load Tool Details Only When Needed

settings.label: Refresh each server's tool list every
settings.desc: It also refreshes when you change a server or ask for it.

settings.label: Add secrets only when a request is sent
settings.desc: Approved secrets are attached at the last moment, hidden in logs, and can never widen access.

settings.label: Show server status around the app
settings.desc: A small connected or disconnected mark wherever server tools appear.
search: Show Server Status in the App

settings.label: Inspect Effective Server Config
settings.desc: A read-only view of exactly what settings each server ended up with, where each value came from, and its sign-in state.

settings.label: Look for updates automatically
settings.desc: You can still check at any time.

settings.label: Keep content up to date
settings.desc: Templates, personas and presets from the catalog.

settings.label: How often to look
settings.desc: Only matters while automatic checks are on.

settings.label: Release channel
settings.desc: Stable is well tested; the others get features sooner.

settings.label: Reset settings to defaults
settings.desc: Pick one setting, a section or everything; you see it first.

settings.label: Save settings to a file
settings.desc: Passwords, keys and sign-ins are never included.

settings.label: Load settings from a file
settings.desc: You see every change before anything is applied.

settings.label: Record extra detail
settings.desc: Slows things a little; turn on only while chasing a problem.

settings.label: How much the logs record
settings.desc: More detail helps support but fills the disk faster.

settings.label: Detail in the activity record
settings.desc: Full keeps more but is harder to read.

settings.label: Show the app's working files
settings.desc: Temporary files made while running; for odd behavior only.

settings.label: Cursor app location
settings.desc: Only if you also use the Cursor app on your server.

settings.label: Claude Code app location
settings.desc: Normally found automatically. Set a manual path only if the app cannot find your Claude Code install; bad paths fail immediately.

settings.label: Find installed apps again
settings.desc: Re-searches your computer for coding apps from scratch, ignoring remembered locations. Use after installing or moving an app.

settings.label: Check the app's parts match at startup
settings.desc: Stops with a clear message if they don't.

settings.label: Drawing engine
settings.desc: Change only if you see visual glitches.

settings.label: Open read-only if another copy is running
settings.desc: Stops two copies from overwriting each other.

settings.label: Settings file format
settings.desc: How settings are written to disk; any of them loads.

settings.label: Also load old settings file names
settings.desc: For projects made with older versions.

settings.label: Warn about changes that raise AI costs
settings.desc: Catches edits that stop prompt caching from working.

settings.label: Chats
settings.desc: Chats stay until you delete them; the two rows below archive and recover them.

settings.label: Goal and run records
settings.desc: In days; at least 365.

settings.label: Diagnostic logs
settings.desc: In days; at least 30.

settings.label: Released safe points
settings.desc: In days; at least 90.

settings.label: Recent terminal runs
settings.desc: Always kept, whatever the logs rule says.

settings.label: Ask for storage compaction
settings.desc: The storage service decides what can be compacted.

settings.label: See holds and quarantined values
settings.desc: Read only; nothing is changed.

settings.label: How work in progress looks
settings.desc: Choose Orbit or the compact Step Rail Simple presentation. The chat and Settings use the same preference.

settings.label: Name new chats
settings.desc: Choose automatic naming, no automatic name, or a model. A name uses the first message only; renaming the chat yourself keeps your name.

settings.label: Explain technical terms in chats
settings.desc: Default at the application or project scope; a chat's own switch wins.

settings.label: Plan depth
settings.desc: Quick sketches fast; Thorough looks carefully first.

settings.label: Deep Plan depth
settings.desc: BrainStorm adds several thinkers who debate and vote.

settings.label: Start Deep Plans with Grill Me
settings.desc: Lets it ask you more questions first; change it per plan.

settings.label: Export plans as
settings.desc: Both formats stay available on every plan.

settings.label: Keep what I was typing
settings.desc: Unsent text stays in each chat when you switch or close.

settings.label: Crew size
settings.desc: Used when the default lineup is empty; a lineup sets the size itself.

settings.label: Who leads
settings.desc: Who directs the Crew: the assistant you are already talking to, a dedicated coordinator teammate, or nobody (each member works its own assignment).

settings.label: How work is shared
settings.desc: How work is handed out: the manager directs it, members claim it, or everyone gets the same task for comparison.

settings.label: Members working at once
settings.desc: The server may allow fewer.

settings.label: Offer a crew for big requests
settings.desc: It only suggests; nothing starts until you confirm.

settings.label: Offer when a request looks
settings.desc: How complex a request has to look before Crew Auto offers a Crew.

settings.label: Largest crew it may offer
settings.desc: The largest Crew that Crew Auto may propose without you raising it yourself.

settings.label: Participants
settings.desc: Used when the lineup is empty; a lineup sets the number itself.

settings.label: Questions it may ask you
settings.desc: The most questions a BrainStorm may ask you before it plans (20). Grill Me raises this by its own extension, so the Grill Me total is 45.

settings.label: Extra questions in Grill Me
settings.desc: The Grill Me question extension: adds to a Plan or BrainStorm base, and is the whole question maximum in a Crew or Chat Room (default 25). The existing assistant, coordinator or moderator interviews you and shows what was agreed for confirmation; Wrap up can end the interview earlier.

settings.label: Quick plan
settings.desc: Grill Me adds more (set in Personas › Crews).

settings.label: Standard plan
settings.desc: Grill Me adds more (set in Personas › Crews).

settings.label: Thorough plan
settings.desc: Grill Me adds more (set in Personas › Crews).

settings.label: Deep Plan, Thorough
settings.desc: Grill Me adds more (set in Personas › Crews).

settings.label: Deep Plan, Exhaustive
settings.desc: Grill Me adds more (set in Personas › Crews).

settings.label: Research outside the project
settings.desc: How hard a BrainStorm researches outside your project. It stays read-only against your code either way.

settings.label: Independent Proposals First
settings.desc: Each participant writes its own proposal before anyone sees the others, so debate starts from genuinely different positions instead of the first idea.

settings.label: BrainStorm Debate Rounds
settings.desc: How many rounds of evidence-driven debate run before voting.

settings.label: How the group decides
settings.desc: How the group decides: weighted by evidence, a plain majority, or the coordinator adjudicates.

settings.label: Keep the losing ideas in the plan
settings.desc: Records the positions that lost the vote in the final Plan, so a rejected option is visible rather than erased.

settings.label: Reviewers
settings.desc: Whether Review runs one fresh reviewer or several independent passes that compare findings afterwards.

settings.label: How many reviewers
settings.desc: From 1 to 8. The same model may repeat.

settings.label: Blind First Pass
settings.desc: Reviewers cannot see each other's findings on the first pass, so agreement means something. They exchange findings only afterwards.

settings.label: Compare Findings
settings.desc: After the blind passes, reviewers see each other's findings and mark agreement or disagreement.

settings.label: Keep Review Dissent
settings.desc: Keeps a finding that only one reviewer stood behind, marked as disputed rather than dropped.

settings.label: Review can fix things
settings.desc: Always off: review reports, fixing is a separate step.

settings.label: Participants
settings.desc: Used when the lineup is empty; a lineup sets the number itself.

settings.label: Taking turns
settings.desc: How the room takes turns: moderated by one participant, strict round-robin, or free-for-all.

settings.label: Rounds before a summary
settings.desc: How many rounds a room runs before it stops and offers a summary.

settings.label: Pause between rounds
settings.desc: Wait after each Chat Room round for Next Round. Off runs the rounds automatically. Copied into the setup sheet; later default changes do not alter a committed room.

settings.label: Advisor
settings.desc: Auto checks in at key moments. Always watching checks in all the time.

settings.label: Model it uses
settings.desc: Its usage is shown separately from your main work.

settings.label: How it talks
settings.desc: Critical Advisor is blunt about risk. Add your own under Personas.

settings.label: How readily it speaks up
settings.desc: How readily elastic review triggers fire. Balanced is the default. Sensitivity does not filter severity, disable required checks, or bypass held-finding reconfirmation.

settings.label: Time to catch up on missed work
settings.desc: After this it skips ahead to what is happening now.

settings.label: Quiet turns after advice
settings.desc: So it does not repeat itself.

settings.label: Keep the advisor's conversation
settings.desc: Lets you open it and see why it said something.

settings.label: Tidy its own notes when this full
settings.desc: 50 to 95%. It never touches your conversation.

settings.label: Stop starting big work before a window closes
settings.desc: No new big step starts this close to the end, so the current one can finish.

settings.label: If a scheduled run is missed
settings.desc: What happens when a scheduled time passes while the app is closed: hold it for you, send at the next opportunity, or cancel after the grace period.

settings.label: Still run if late by up to
settings.desc: A late run still starts if it is no later than this.

settings.label: Resume paused work in the next window
settings.desc: Picks paused work back up when the next execution window opens. A manual Stop or Pause always wins over this.

settings.label: Pick up paused work when usage resets
settings.desc: Work you paused yourself always stays paused.

settings.label: Daylight saving
settings.desc: Runs keep local clock time; read only.

settings.label: Screenshot button captures
settings.desc: Whether the screenshot button captures just what you can see or the whole scrolling page.

settings.label: After picking a page element
settings.desc: What happens when you pick a component: send it straight away, add it to a numbered list in the composer, or insert it at your cursor. Remembers whichever you used last.
settings.default: Last used, starting with Send now
settings.recommended: Last used, starting with Send now

settings.label: Attach a picture of the element
settings.desc: Attaches a cropped picture of the component alongside its structure and styles.

settings.label: Let the assistant open DevTools
settings.desc: Whether the assistant may open DevTools in the ordinary internal browser. The protected sign-in browser is never included and stays yours alone.

settings.label: Keep a working notebook
settings.desc: Saves findings and dead ends during long tasks.

settings.label: Add a short recap when work resumes
settings.desc: A brief 'where we were' note after a fresh start.

settings.label: Recap size limit
settings.desc: Most tokens the recap may use.

settings.label: Notebook space per reply
settings.desc: Most tokens of notebook text added to one reply.

settings.label: Switch editor colors with light and dark
settings.desc: When the app changes between light and dark, a scheme you picked for the editor swaps for its family's other version, such as Catppuccin Latte and Mocha. Follow look always does.

settings.label: Bracket pair colors
settings.desc: Matching brackets share a color, a new one at each depth.

settings.label: Editor text contrast
settings.desc: 7:1 moves dim colors lighter or darker; their hue stays.

settings.label: Comments in italics
settings.desc: Draws comments in the face's italic. Follow look uses the look's own style: italic in most looks, upright in Retro dark.

settings.label: Keywords in bold
settings.desc: Draws keywords heavier than the rest of the code. Follow look uses the look's own weight: bold in Retro and NieR Mode, regular elsewhere.

settings.label: Editor text weight
settings.desc: JetBrains Mono 400 to 800, Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono 200 to 800.

settings.label: Editor letter spacing
settings.desc: Extra space between characters of code, in pixels. Columns stay aligned, since every character takes the same width.

settings.label: Ligatures
settings.desc: Joins -> and != into one symbol where the font has them.

settings.label: Caret shape
settings.desc: The shape of the editor's caret. Follow look uses the look's own: a line in most looks, a block in Retro.

settings.label: Caret width
settings.desc: How thick the line caret is, in pixels.

settings.label: Caret blink
settings.desc: How the caret blinks: on and off, fading, growing from its middle, or not at all. Reduce motion keeps it solid.

settings.label: Caret movement
settings.desc: Whether the caret jumps to where it goes or glides there. Typing never waits for it. Reduce motion makes it jump.

settings.label: Trail when the caret jumps
settings.desc: Only for jumps of several lines you did not click.

settings.label: Count lines from the caret
settings.desc: Line numbers count up and down from the caret's line, which keeps its own number.

settings.label: Highlight the current line
settings.desc: How the caret's line stands out: a band across the line and a brighter number, the band only, the number only, or nothing.

settings.label: Indent guides
settings.desc: Thin vertical lines at each level of indentation. Rainbow gives each level its own color.

settings.label: Light the guide of the block I'm in
settings.desc: With indent guides on, the guide of the block that holds the caret is drawn brighter.

settings.label: Show spaces
settings.desc: Marks spaces with faint dots: between words where there are several, only in the selection, only at the ends of lines, or everywhere.

settings.label: Rulers
settings.desc: Faint lines at the columns lines should stay within.

settings.label: Wrap long lines at
settings.desc: Where wrapped lines break: at the edge of the editor, or at a column (or the edge, if that comes first). Applies while Wrap Long Lines is on.

settings.label: Sticky scroll lines
settings.desc: The most enclosing lines sticky scroll keeps in view, from 1 to 5.

settings.label: Smooth scrolling
settings.desc: Scrolling with the wheel or by a page glides instead of jumping. Follow look uses the look's own: on in Friendly and Glass. Reduce motion turns it off.

settings.label: Lines arrive when a file opens
settings.desc: The first screen of a file arrives line by line from the top, quickly. Off shows it at once. Reduce motion always shows it at once.

settings.label: Scroll past the last line
settings.desc: How far you can scroll below the last line, so it need not sit at the bottom edge.

settings.label: Fade editors I'm not in
settings.desc: When you are working in another panel, editors you are not in fade back a little, as Dim Terminals I'm Not In does for terminals.

settings.label: Scanlines
settings.desc: Thin still lines across the code, like an old monitor.

settings.label: Text glow
settings.desc: A soft glow around code in its own color.

settings.label: Tab size
settings.desc: Columns in a level of indentation. A file with its own keeps it while the editor follows it.

settings.label: Indent with
settings.desc: What a new level is made of in a file that doesn't already say, and in every file while Follow the file's indentation is off. A tab is drawn and copied as a tab.

settings.label: Follow the file's indentation
settings.desc: A file indented with 2 spaces keeps 2; one indented with tabs keeps tabs. Off, Indent with and Tab size decide in every file.

settings.label: Token colours
settings.desc: One kind of word in one scheme, as scheme/kind: #rrggbb. Set them in the editor's Customize screen, under Colors.

settings.label: Background Strength
settings.desc: How strongly a built-in design shows, from 0 to 1; it never goes so far that text stops being readable.

settings.label: Pattern Size
settings.desc: Size of a terminal pattern, for every Pattern design but Paper; the design stays in the current scheme.

settings.label: Background Motion
settings.desc: Applies only to a moving design, and only in the terminal you are in; it stops when that terminal is idle or hidden, on battery saver and under Reduce Animations.

settings.label: Picture Fit
settings.desc: How a custom terminal picture fits its screen.

settings.label: Less colour
settings.desc: How much colour a custom picture loses, 0–1: full colour, half or grey, half by default.

settings.label: Terminal Bezel
settings.desc: A housing around the terminal, off by default: Slim is a thin rim, and Monitor a monitor case that catches the screen's light, on its own or with Full CRT.

settings.label: Bezel Width
settings.desc: 2–48 px, or the style default: Slim 6 px and Monitor 24 px. No bezel is enabled by changing width.

settings.label: Bezel Material
settings.desc: What the bezel is made of. Follow look uses the look's own material; in NieR Mode that is a flat ink frame.

settings.label: Bezel Reflection
settings.desc: How much of the screen the bezel gives back: Off, Low, Medium or High, starting at the material's own level, which Auto keeps. Not offered on NieR's own ink frame.

settings.label: Phosphor Mask
settings.desc: Full CRT's phosphor mask: an aperture grille of three device pixels to a triad, drawn at every display density. Off by default.

settings.label: Show thinking
settings.desc: While it thinks opens the reasoning supplied by the model while it works, then folds it away. Always open keeps that reasoning visible. This changes only what is shown, never a reply.

settings.label: Lines shown while thinking
settings.desc: How much of the reasoning supplied by the model While it thinks keeps in view as it streams: the latest lines, with older ones fading at the top. Always open shows all of it. This changes only what is shown, never a reply.
